rationale: Twenty-four parts at their 896-line/98,304-byte bound total 21,504 lines against a 9,600-line aggregate. Parts are canonical evidence of one active tree and can only be added, so the aggregate is reachable by compliant writing with no compliant exit (ADR 0032).

Nine collection indexes at their 384-line/65,536-byte per-file bound total 3,456 lines, above the 1,024-line aggregate. One index exists per governed collection and none is ever retired, so the aggregate had no compliant exit (ADR 0032).
Forty pages at their 1,200-line/49,152-byte bound total 48,000 lines against a 4,000-line aggregate. Pages are managed canonical material with no declared retirement route (ADR 0032).
Sixteen parts at their 896-line/98,304-byte bound total 14,336 lines against a 6,144-line aggregate, the same shape as the active parts surface it mirrors (ADR 0032).

Thirty-two packets at their 512-line/32,768-byte bound total 16,384 lines against a 5,000-line aggregate. A packet is a permanent record of an exchange with the downstream consumer and has no declared retirement route (ADR 0032).

Two hundred fifty-six fixtures at their 80-line/8,192-byte bound total 20,480 lines against a 4,000-line aggregate. Bench fixtures are permanent — the 156/156 oracle depends on them — so no fixture may be deleted to recover the total (ADR 0032).
Eight bundle files at their 512-line/32,768-byte bound total 4,096 lines against a 2,000-line aggregate. The bundle is the portable Knowledge Map standard and its files are permanent (ADR 0032).

Sixty-four records at their 640-line/65,536-byte bound total 40,960 lines against a 12,000-line aggregate. Records are dated measurement evidence that is never deleted, and the file count is already at 81.2% with its own capacity remedy (ADR 0032).

One hundred sixty trees at their 3,000-line/278,528-byte bound total 480,000 lines against a 40,000-line aggregate, which binds at a 250-line mean against a measured 229.7 — so raising the file capacity its 81.9% warning calls for would have produced capacity that could not be used (ADR 0032).

The 16 declared standard files may each be 700 lines and 65,536 bytes, so a corpus of legal standards could total 11,200 lines the 3,000-line aggregate would refuse. Members are permanent bootstrap standards that are never deleted or rolled, so the count is the dimension with a remedy (ADR 0032).
